CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for a follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed but generally positive response to the current treatment regimen. He notes that his sleep quality has improved slightly, with an average of 8 hours per night; however, he still encounters difficulty with sleep onset, particularly on nights preceding demanding workdays. The trazodone at 75 mg continues to assist with nocturnal awakenings, but he expresses concern regarding the increased frequency of early morning awakenings, which often leave him feeling unrefreshed.
Regarding his persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith reports a modest enhancement in his daytime energy levels, attributing this improvement to his continued engagement in mindfulness practices and regular yoga sessions. Despite this, he still experiences considerable fatigue during peak work periods, describing it as mentally draining. His headache symptoms have shown slight variability; he reports occurrences approximately 2-3 times per week, with an intensity fluctuating between 4-6 out of 10. He has been utilizing ibuprofen 400 mg approximately 3-4 times weekly for headache relief, which he finds moderately effective but remains concerned about his reliance on this medication.
Mr. Smith continues to adhere to his holistic treatment plan, including ongoing acupuncture sessions and yoga classes. He has also maintained his participation in cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions, which he feels have been beneficial in managing his anxiety, particularly in relation to work stressors. He expresses a desire to further refine his coping strategies to better manage the pressures associated with his job.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (usage slightly decreased) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Topiramate 25 mg daily (titration considered) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that the pressure from project deadlines remains a significant stressor. He actively participates in yoga and meditation, which he finds helpful. He abstains from alcohol and follows a primarily plant-based diet, although he admits to occasionally indulging in processed foods during particularly stressful weeks.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep initiation difficulties persist; anxiety is stable with slight improvements noted; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has decreased; intensity fluctuates; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 68 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, and appears slightly fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce tapering of lorazepam use as needed. Encourage ongoing cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions to enhance coping strategies for work-related stress. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 75 mg; continue melatonin at 10 mg; explore sleep hygiene strategies and consider a sleep study if sleep onset issues persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly. Given the slight decrease in headache frequency and intensity, continue topiramate at 25 mg daily, with plans to reassess in the next visit. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued physical activity and mindfulness practices. Refer to a nutritionist for dietary optimization, particularly during high-stress periods.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-09-01 to assess ongoing symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
